title: Value vs Reference Types in C#

scenes.say: Struct or class? Why does that choice matter in C sharp interviews?
Value types like structs and ints store their data directly. Reference types like classes and records just store a reference to the data.
When you assign an int to an object, C sharp wraps the value in a reference type. This is called boxing.

scenes.label: Records
scenes.sub: Records are reference types with value-based equality.
scenes.say: Records are reference types, but they compare by value, not by reference. That's handy for equality checks.

scenes.question: Where is a value type stored?
scenes.right: It depends—can be stack or heap
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Value types aren't always on the stack. They can live on the heap too, like inside a class or when boxed.
